text.p: AutoImmune Inc, Friday it has begun further restructuring to reduce the company's full-time staff to about 20 employees from 50 over the next few months.

The company, a biopharmaceutical company developing a new class of drug therapies for the treatment of autoimmune diseases, said said it plans to take a one-time restructuring charge of about $2.7 million in the current quarter.
It said the restructuring will be completed by the end of the third quarter, resulting in a reduction of net quarterly spending to about $1.5 million, plus the cost of any new clinical trials.
"This restructuring will provide the financial flexibility to pursue a number of strategic options, including the full-scale development of Colloral," said Chief Executive Robert Bishop.
A month ago AutoImmune said two Colloral Phase II rheumatoid arthritis trials had demonstrated positive trends but did not show statistical significance versus placebo.
At that time, the company said the drug may require further development before entering Phase III trials.
Today's statement said preliminary data from a third Phase II active control trial of Colloral are expected this summer.
Also expected this summer are results from Magnetic Resonance Imaging scans from the Myloral Phase III trial.
Following analysis of the additional Myloral and Colloral data, the company will evaluate the next development steps for these two products, it said.

Bishop said, "Clinical activities are continuing with our partner in the diabetes field, Eli Lilly and Co, which currently has three Phase II trials of AI-401 under way, and our Phase I/II trial for the prevention of organ transplant rejection is ongoing at Brigham and Women's Hospital."
As of March 31, AutoImmune had cash and marketable securities of $43.4 million, or $2.65 per share.
